carry_forward_bullets: The body schema a rule names (name@pkg.Message) is carried to the row as body_schema and read by nothing. The door that turns a schema into field names, and the one that builds a protobuf body from JSON, are later steps; the body is today walked schema-less as protobuf and shown under payload_decode in payload coordinates.

Frames are judged in the order the document walks them: flow by flow, in capture order within a flow. A slot whose frames are spread over two flows (one sender and key over two connections) is judged flow by flow and not in time order. Only a Push carrying a put is a frame; a query or a reply under a profile key is not judged, and a Push whose key did not resolve (an id the capture never saw declared) is not judged and moves no slot.

A row a ceiling holds back is not judged. The cap drops the tail of a flow, so the verdicts of the rows that are written are unaffected, but a slot shared with a later flow would miss them. A live handle recomputes every slot from the rows it still holds on each call, so after a front trim the oldest retained frame of a slot reads as its first reception; the e2e cells are listed among the cells an issued row may read differently later.

Which sender a frame has is the zid announced on the link, so a capture that began after the handshake has no counter verdicts at all under a profile that separates senders. Whether the reference receiver separates senders only when it is configured to is not settled for a deployment; the profile option by_zid:false models the pooled reading.

A profile cannot say a rule that depends on a value. The sender cell inside the header is deliberately not a slot axis, and the timeout and CRC rules are read from the consumer's written specification only; nothing ran on the consumer's own constants.
The hosted runners have not run any of it, and the since door's re-walk of passed rows costs a walk per passed row when a profile rule exists; it was not measured on a large capture.

begin_frame writes a ten-byte VLE for a sequence number from 2^63, where the codec and upstream end a VLE at nine bytes; no session reaches it, because the ring mask stops at 63 bits, and build_frame_wire does not share it.

Round 3153.decision_summary: The wrap door of the end-to-end protection mechanism now takes its body as a description instead of bytes. A consumer that sends protobuf in a protected frame had to serialize the body itself and so held a second writer of the wire format beside the library's. The values text of wz_dissect_e2e_wrap may now carry an @body member (a .proto file list, a root file, a message name, the field values), and the library's protobuf writer builds the bytes that the header, CRC and length are put around. It is a key of the existing description text and not a new symbol, so the ABI does not move, and no header field can be called @body, so a text without it reads as before. Document e2e_wrap moved to revision 2. A refusal of the writer is the door's own refusal with the writer's diagnostic and a pointer into the caller's text, and no frame is built around a refused body. The message name is the string a profile rule carries as body_schema.

Round 3158.decision_summary: This round starts the transmit half of the runtime-zero-copy atom at its base. ARCHITECTURE section 9.1 says the codec writes directly into a pool slot and the link then sends that slot. Measured against the code, nothing could do that: every outbound encoder was written against a VecSink over a growable Vec, so each outgoing frame on the immediate and lowlatency paths allocated a vector of its own, and on the batching path the stage buffer is taken at every flush and re-reserved for the next frame, one allocation per batch; and no destination other than a Vec could be handed to an encoder at all. The generated pools already carry the whole transmit arc (acquire for encode, arm tx, start tx, tx complete) and the link write door already takes borrowed bytes, so the missing piece is the encoder side. This round adds it without moving any behavior. A TxBuf trait names what an encoder needs of its destination: its length, a rollback, the written bytes, and an append that may refuse. Vec<u8> implements it and cannot refuse. SliceTxBuf implements it over a borrowed fixed slice, which is what a pool slot's storage is, and refuses a write past the end with BufferOverflow instead of panicking. TxSink adapts any TxBuf to the codec's sink, so the body encoders are written once against one sink type and the choice of destination does not multiply their instantiations. The grade does not move: no consumer hands a slot to these encoders yet.

Round 3159.decision_summary: This round finishes the session side of the transmit half of runtime-zero-copy and lands the first real lender. ARCHITECTURE section 9.1 has the codec write directly into a buffer that the link then sends. Round 3158 made every encoder write to a TxBuf; this round decides who owns the buffer. Measured against the code, the session cannot own it: the stream driver builds a second framed Vec from the encoded bytes and hands it to its writer task by ownership, a multilink session has one link per pool, and only the link knows what its DMA domain needs in front of the payload. So the link lends and the session encodes. BoxedLinkDriver gains four defaulted methods (acquire a slot, name its storage, send it, abort it) and a grant that states the headroom the link wants in front of the frame; every existing driver keeps the defaults, which lend nothing. A TxLease is a lent slot seen as a TxBuf and gives the slot back if dropped unsent. The immediate send path tries a lease before the heap encode and falls back to the heap, with the sequence number already minted, when the link lends nothing, has no free slot, the encode overflows the slot, or the frame needs fragmenting. The wanted size is a hint, not a promise. emit_on_link stays the single funnel for stamping, compression, statistics and liveness. The stream driver now lends a Vec with the framing prefix room in front, writes the prefix in place and gives the filled Vec to the writer queue by ownership, which turns two allocations and a copy per frame into one allocation. The reconnect swap seams forward the lend and remember which link lent each slot, so a swap during an encode sends and aborts on the link that lent the slot instead of presenting its slot number to a stranger. The atom is not yet complete: the writer queue still carries Vec items, the lowlatency path and the batching stage buffer do not lend, and the microcontroller side still copies three times after the encoder.

carry_forward_bullets: Note for the SCE owner: the generator offers no checked-read primitive for a bytes parameter. data[i] in an algorithm body lowers to an unchecked index (data[(i) as usize]), so every bound had to be written by hand in the loop condition, and the integer-range analysis did not flag the missing bound. Two requests: a checked read (for example data.get(i) yielding a fallible value, or a foreach-with-index that cannot run past the input), and a diagnostic when a bytes parameter is indexed by an expression the analysis cannot prove less than len(data). The same generator lowers len(data) to a cast of the usize length into the declared variable type, which clips silently when that type is narrower (uint16 clipped at 65536); a diagnostic for a narrowing len() init would have caught it.

carry_forward_bullets: Still not recovered, by design, each held by a test: an INIT whose body reached the device but whose 0x00 end marker has not (the unterminated tail is never searched, since its end is unknown and what arrives after the flush completes it; closing this would mean keeping the tail across the flush and deciding whether it is stale, which the contract does not allow today); and an INIT the line corrupted (its CRC fails at every offset). A peer that controls the wire can send an INIT anyway, so the search adds no new attack surface.

Open decision for the owner: the search accepts the first matching offset in a span (earliest start, longest frame). A frame whose payload deliberately embeds a valid INIT frame as its tail could be mistaken for an INIT only by grinding a payload whose CRC bytes complete one, which an on-wire attacker could do more simply by sending the INIT.

The accept flush reads at most 1 MiB; the worst-case search over that is about 1.6e9 byte steps and was not timed. If a measurement is wanted, the cheap tightening is to prune offsets whose decoded length disagrees with the length field read from the first three decoded bytes before the full decode.

Round 3163.decision_summary: The accept flush kept an INIT already on the wire, but one glued to stale bytes that no 0x00 closed was lost: a frame is COBS(body) 0x00 with only the end marked (no leading delimiter), pico reads to the first 0x00 and drops the whole span on a CRC failure, and upstream's z-serial does the same, so the fragment and the INIT are one span. A responder RESET would wake the initiator but departs from upstream, so the wire is left unchanged. Instead, for the accept-time flush only, each 0x00-terminated span is searched for the frame that ends at its 0x00 from every start offset; a candidate is accepted only if it is a well-formed COBS sequence landing on the span end, passes the length and CRC32 checks and carries a responder INIT header (false accept below 2^-32 per offset, at most 1516 offsets per span). The steady-state reader still drops the span as pico does. Unrecoverable and pinned: an INIT whose 0x00 has not arrived, and a corrupted INIT.

Round 3167.decision_summary: This round builds the microcontroller transmit chain of runtime-zero-copy from the Ethernet controller up to the session, so that a frame the session encodes is read by the DMA from where it was written. Round 3159 settled that the link lends the buffer; on the microcontroller profile the link is lwIP over a MAC, and three layers copied after the encoder: the driver allocated a pbuf and copied the frame in, the C shim flattened the pbuf chain into a static buffer, and the MAC copied that into its ring. The chain is now cut at each of them without changing a byte on the wire. At the bottom the EthernetMac seam gains transmit_gather and reap_tx, with a copying default so no other MAC changes, and the CYT4BF MAC overrides them with the Cadence driver's own multi-buffer protocol, read from the vendor's reference source: the first descriptor of a frame is written held, the rest follow, the first is released last, and completion is read only from the first descriptor, whose later siblings software marks used itself. A frame queued in place owes its caller a report, and reap_tx is the only place such a frame is reclaimed, so a caller that never reaps is refused once the ring is full, which is the right back-pressure on memory it has not been given back; a transmit error loses the frame to the wire but still frees its memory. In the middle the C shim holds a reference on the pbuf chain it hands the MAC piece by piece and drops it when the MAC reports the frame done, falling back to the old flat copy for a chain of many pieces or a full table of held chains, and the Rust adapter offers pieces only to a MAC that says it queues in place, because the trait default would put a 1.5 KB buffer on the stack. At the top the lwIP link driver lends the payload of a transport-layer pbuf, which already has room in front of it for the UDP, IP and Ethernet headers, so the session encodes with no headroom and the frame reaches the MAC as one contiguous piece. The shim counts the payload pbufs it lends so that a leak shows on the host port, where lwIP keeps no statistics, because a per-datagram pbuf leak has run an MCU heap dry here before. The new driver tests run in every lwIP leg of the exact-count lanes, so thirteen count guards move with them. This is BUILT and not HARDWARE: the controller model is written from the same documents as the driver, the board's cache clean is a no-op that assumes non-cacheable memory, and the kit has not been flashed.

Round 3169.decision_summary: This round builds the first two thirds of the microcontroller receive path, makes the AP transmit steady state allocation-free, and corrects the record of the one remaining atom. After Round 3167 the transmit chain no longer copied, but a received frame was still copied three times before the session saw it: the MAC copied it out of its ring, the shim copied it into a pbuf, and the socket copied the datagram into an owned slot. The first two are now cut. The EthernetMac seam gains receive_loan and return_rx, with a default that lends nothing so no other MAC changes, and the CYT4BF MAC lends the frame where the controller wrote it and withholds that buffer from the controller until it is returned. Two things make withholding safe and are pinned: a ring that comes all the way round to a lent buffer must read it as nothing waiting, because its descriptor still says finished and the stack already holds that frame, and re-arming the whole ring after a link change must leave a lent buffer alone. In the shim a lent frame is wrapped in a custom pbuf that points at it, and the pbuf's free callback returns the buffer, so lwIP reads the frame in place and the buffer is given back when the last reference drops, which for a fragment parked in reassembly is long after the input call returned. A return that happens while the MAC is borrowed is parked and given back by the next poll instead of aliasing it, and a frame the shim cannot wrap, because its table of lent frames is full or the port has no custom pbufs, takes the copying input and is returned at once. The third copy, in the socket's receive callback, is the MCU profile's owned form and is not touched. On the AP, the stream driver already lent a vector with the framing prefix room, which left one allocation per frame; the writer task now returns each buffer it has written to a small bounded pool kept in the shared lane state, four buffers of at most 16 KiB, and the next lend draws from it, so a link in steady state allocates none, and an abandoned lend returns its buffer too. A first version of the abandoned-lend test compared buffer addresses and still passed with the return removed, because the allocator hands a freed buffer's address to the next request; the pool is now read directly, and the same break turns the test red. The runtime-zero-copy reason still said the transmit path of section 9.1 was untouched and that send_blocking encodes into a fresh vector, and the reason is what the next session reads to decide what to build, so an UPDATE paragraph for Rounds 3159 to 3169 is appended to it with the earlier segments kept as they were: the primitive replaces the whole field, so the new text was assembled from the stored one by a program and the stored result was read back and compared with what was sent, with every earlier UPDATE marker checked present. The paragraph states what is built, what each piece is witnessed by, and what it does not retire, each re-measured against the code, and one clause I first wrote, that the acquire-for-encode edge has no caller, was wrong because the receive-side staging calls it and was narrowed before the text was stored. The grade stays PARTIAL and the audit still lists this atom as the only remaining work.

Round 3171.decision_summary: This round recovers, at its base, the 1456 bytes of ROM that Round 3170 re-baselined instead of removing. Round 3170 recorded that the MCU multicast image pays for the transmit buffer seam without using it and named the carry as a sink generic over the buffer. Reading the code before building it showed that carry to be insufficient, and the reasons are the design: the cost is fallibility (a vector's push cannot fail, so the codec's error branch after every write folds away; a write through a dyn TxBuf sink can fail, so the branch stays in every encoder); the body encoders are closures of one fixed sink type, which a generic sink does not change; the lend attempt stays reachable in the multicast image because the link a session writes to is a trait object, so a generic form would link both instantiations; and the image links the lwIP session shell, so a feature that shell enables is on in the image. So the decision is that only the composition can say a slot is never lent. The session crate gains a feature, transport-tx-lend, off by default, that gates the lend attempt and selects the encoders' buffer type through one alias (the vector, or dyn TxBuf), with the sink generic over its buffer so no encoder changed. Who turns it on is derived from who lends, not chosen: the AP runtime unconditionally (its writer lends), the unicast MCU acceptor topology, the MCU admin node and the Zephyr admin node's lwIP backend (their link is the lwIP UDP driver, which lends); the multicast image, whose driver never lends, does not. The seam's own tests stay on in each crate's test build through a dev-dependency, so the lending form stays tested where it is the subject. The alternative of leaving the regression inside a re-baselined band was rejected: 1308 bytes is five times the band that exists to notice growth, and the owner's rule is to fix the base.

Round 3173.decision_summary: Item 861: the premise is half wrong. bindgen has four consumers in the crates workspace (librocksdb-sys, lwip-sys, zenoh-pico-sys, io-uring) above 29 of 66 members, plus libxml in xtask and in SCE's workspace, so libclang-dev and clang are needed on 19 of 20 jobs. The register's remedy, deriving each job's reach from census text, is unsound both ways: validate-codegen's gates quote every member name in their selftests (false need), and verdict-legs names no crate (its cargo test set is chosen at run time and includes wz-replay, which reaches a consumer), so a text derivation would drop a package it needs. Decided: validate-codegen was MEASURED to compile nothing (13 layers under a cargo that refuses compiling verbs: only metadata and tree calls), so it drops both packages; the census pins its layer set, bars compiling lines in those layers, and gains a selftest and a measure mode. The runner image already carries libclang, so nothing reddens; the gain is bytes on a cold apt cache.

A moved file, a missing row, an orphan row, a duplicate or malformed row all fail; a population of zero is normal and passes. The population is derived (store plus the census's own citation resolver, now shared as resolve_citation). Deviations: register said PARTIAL reasons only, this also covers UNBUILT and UNVERIFIED, the tags that assert remaining work; granularity is the whole file. A pin is not evidence the reason is true and the doc says so. Seeded 13 rows for runtime-zero-copy as seed, meaning taken, not read.

1. Assertions are not barriers. `captured.contains("...")` checks after a wait (and negative ones, `!captured.contains`) read the same producer text and are not graded. A negative assertion on text nobody prints is a vacuous test, a separate defect. Exact next step: extend the needle reader to `.contains(` on a captured string inside the same e2e functions, positive form first, and add a positive-control rule for the negative form.

2. Coverage is a necessary condition, not a sufficient one: a needle can be covered by a literal printed somewhere other than where the test looks. The run prints how many template needles rest on fewer than 4 literal characters (0 today). Closing the gap needs the spawn data flow (which binary writes into which capture), which this gate does not model.

3. Producers that are values with whitespace inside a needle (the face-up line, the plugin-section lines) are declared with a template, not searched. If more of them appear, consider letting a wz format argument that is an if/else of literals expand the template.

4. Foreign text is declared, not verified, unless it carries an upstream citation; zenoh-c example text has no pinned source in this tree to cite. First hosted C0 run after this lands: read the step by job; the gate needs vendor/zenoh-pico in that job.

scripts/lib/barrier_needle_gate.py (new)

Needles: wait_for_substring (needle index read from its own definition per crate) and wrappers derived to a fixed point (a fn forwarding one of its parameters as the needle). A fn that also hands the parameter to a program (.arg/.args/.env/write/put/publish/send...) directly or through a crate fn is a send-and-wait fn: its callers' values are the test's own and are not graded.

Readable needle forms: literal, format! (each literal piece), identifier bound by let, for .. in [..], tuple let / tuple for over a literal table or a const table, parameter, const (also use ... as alias, other file of the crate), array of those, a call to a crate fn (its literals), if/else. Anything else is UNREADABLE and fails.

Producers: literals of crates/*/src (not test-support crates, cfg(test) items and test module files excluded), tracked C sources, vendored pico, Rust literals carrying printf( or #include (probes), printf formats inside scripts (the pico patch heredoc).

Match: plain containment in one literal segment, or a bit-parallel NFA over the template (checked equal to an exact dict NFA in the selftest): placeholders print one non-space token up to 80 characters; the search tier needs 4 literal characters; templates under 8 literal characters are not producers.

Declarations in comments, crate-wide: `barrier-origin: <kind> "<needle>" [-- `path` @ `anchor`]` (kinds zenohd, zenoh-c, zenoh-ext, test-payload; a program kind must be named by the file of the barrier; a citation must share text with the needle and is graded by the existing upstream anchor gate) and `barrier-producer: <path> @ "<template>" for "<needle>"` (the template must occur in that producer file and cover that needle, whitespace allowed in its values). A declaration no barrier of the crate used is stale and fails.

Round 3199.decision_summary: Item 862 reproduced and root-caused in the implementation, not the test. A stress with four sweeping threads read Held(0) after the owner let go 2 times in 60000 owners. collect() took a due chunk off the busy list under the busy lock but advanced its slot generation only after releasing it; a thread that finds the list empty (the owner's Drop, whose chunk a concurrent sweep claimed between the owner's release and its own collect) therefore read Held(0). Round 3210.decision_summary: Whether one program may hold a client session and a multicast peer session at once could only be answered by reading the code, so this round runs it on the AP profile. The two are typestates of one Session type, each built from its own observer, dispatcher and link. The process-wide statics wz-runtime-tokio keeps (runtime pool, SHM registries, and the link-RX table under runtime-zero-copy) are shared by design, and none admits only one session. The first run failed because the test asserted the wrong thing: is_established() reads the bundle's "a session was established here" stamp, which only a reconnect's reset clears. The test now asserts what loss means: the loop returns Terminated and a send is refused as TransportUnavailable. The MCU and Zephyr profiles are not covered. On MCU the multicast loop owns the thread and never pumps the local set the unicast session runs on, and Zephyr has no group link. That work is carried forward.

Round 3218.decision_summary: runtime-zero-copy: re-measured before building. On main the MCU transmit chain already lends an lwIP heap pbuf and the CYT4BF MAC gathers in place, but (1) no TX pool existed and the generated DMA transmit edges had no caller, (2) the T2G image's MAC wrapper forwarded only transmit/receive, so the image never read a frame in place, and (3) the board's cache clean is a no-op, so reading lwIP heap pbufs in place on the kit would be incoherent. The MAC now reads in place only memory its board allows (required Board::reads_in_place; Cyt4bfBoard window). The T2G image gets an overlay placing the pool in .nocache, a BUILT row and steps HW.26 to HW.30. Grade unchanged: no hardware witness.

Round 3223.decision_summary: The 1 of 1200 on hosted Windows (Platform run 38013268899) is the test, not the open. The open is released only after face_up has run (FaceOwed is paid in on_up, and on drop only when face_up refused, which a lone dialler cannot hit), so an empty read needs a face that LEFT the registry. The test's bind-read-drop probe can hand one number to two of its threads; on Linux the second bind is refused and retried, on Windows a wz listener sets SO_REUSEADDR as upstream's does and both binds succeed. A dial is then accepted by the other thread's listener, whose teardown takes the face down before the read. Decided: each round's port comes from free_port, the workspace SSOT that never hands one number twice in a process, and a face to another listener is counted apart from an empty registry. Product listener semantics on Windows are unchanged: wz mirrors upstream's unconditional set_reuseaddr, and moving off it is an owner decision.

Round 3225.decision_summary: This round repays a Layer E red that was attributed to the Round 3217 push and was not caused by it. Hosted run 38013268891 failed one job, Layer E, on a_config_that_states_listen_and_connect_listens_and_dials_on_wz_and_zenoh_pico: the wz arm printed from-the-dialled samples=4 where the real zenoh-pico printed 5. The first reading, written into the acknowledgement of that run, was that the lend implication Round 3217 removed had moved a sample count; measured, it had not. For the binary under test cargo tree shows the session crate's alloc feature enabled directly by wz-runtime-tokio, so dropping the implication leaves its feature set identical, and the same test fails on the tree before the Round 3217 commits. The cause is in the test. The driver is a C program that opens a session, then declares its subscriber, then counts the five Puts the demo publishes; the demo bursts the instant its session reaches Established, which can precede the driver's subscription declaration, and a Put that reaches a peer with no subscription yet is dropped, which is correct protocol behaviour. The reference arm reads 5 because the real zenoh-pico's open returns later, not because it is guaranteed. The repository already documented this race and its remedy in a sibling test, wz_matching_status_driven_by_pico_zsub.rs, which holds its demo's burst with the demo's own pre-burst delay flag so the peer's declaration is strictly first; this test never passed that flag. The decision is the same remedy in the same form: the demo holds its burst for one second, named as a constant with its reason, and the driver's own eight second wait is left alone. The root cause was measured before it was fixed, and the fix was measured against the same method.

carry_forward_bullets: 1. No shipped MCU deploy selects bounded-heapless yet. Switching one is a deploy decision with a measured cost: the observer's registries become inline (each MAX_KEYEXPR_BYTES pattern row is about 256 bytes; the subscriber, queryable, pending-query, inbound-interest, liveliness and token tables together are tens of KiB), and ApplicationLayerObserver::new() is built on the stack before Rc::new moves it. Next step: build the target deploy with its shell crate forwarding wz-session-core/bounded-heapless, run its Layer Q case and read the stack: peak line; place the observer in static storage (memo S5/S6) if the margin is gone.

2. A refused staging is counted, not retried. The counters (SubInterestRefusals, token_interest_chains_refused) are the signal; whether a refused chain is retried at the next drain or the frame is answered in more than one drain is memo section 2 (queues become counted refusals) and needs an owner decision.

4. Over-deep keyexprs (more than 32 chunks) are a conservative no-match on the fixed backing, as on the no-alloc profile; on the growable backing they match.

Round 3229.decision_summary: Step S1 of the fixed-memory MCU plan. Premise re-measured and it reproduced: under alloc, bounded.rs backed BoundedVec/BoundedString with Vec/String, so every caps limit was advisory on every MCU deploy and TableFull was unreachable. A new feature bounded-heapless selects the heapless backing while alloc stays on; it implies nothing and alloc keeps its meaning, so the AP keeps growable collections. Sites whose behaviour differs on the capped backing were derived by compiling with the feature, not listed by hand. The closure wrappers whose expect holds only when the table grows are compiled out under the feature (kept for the crate's own tests and docs). Stagers that swallowed a refused push now stage a reply chain whole or refuse and count it, so no chain is truncated or loses its Final. The liveliness-get table counts an undrained final marker as occupied, closing a replay leak that only a debug_assert guarded. Host-test level only; no deploy was switched.

Round 3231.decision_summary: wz-runtime-tokio treats registrations as infallible (register_sink(..).expect(..) sites and the closure wrappers), which is true only on the growable backing. Cargo feature unification could hand it the fixed backing if any crate in an AP build graph enabled wz-session-core/bounded-heapless, and each of those sites would then panic at the first full table. A compile-time assert on bounded::ENFORCES_CAPACITY makes that graph fail to build with the reason instead. It refuses a misconfiguration and changes nothing on the AP profile.

Round 3237.decision_summary: The kit's copied frames were every frame the session hands the lwIP driver as bytes: the driver lent pool slots only through its slot door, and its byte door (send_blocking, through send_to) sent from a pbuf of lwIP's heap, which the MAC cannot read in place. On the admin node image that is the handshake (InitSyn, InitAck, OpenSyn, OpenAck), the keep-alive cadence and the close; with batching, fragmentation or compression on it is also flushed batches, fragments and compressed batches. The fix is at the one place that owns the pool: send_to copies the bytes into a slot when one fits, so the MAC reads them in place and the lwIP heap is not touched. Encoding those frames straight into a lease in the session was not done: a keep-alive is one byte, a close two, a handshake frame once per session, so the copy left is the size of the encode. A flushed batch keeps the reason's open clause (3). ARP and ICMP stay copied by design.

Round 3238.decision_summary: runtime-zero-copy clause (3) is built behind transport-tx-lend: a batch frame opens in a slot the conduit's link lends, is held across the window's calls as a pointer-free HeldSlot recorded ON THE LENDING LINK, takes each message straight into it (rollback on overflow), and its flush sends the slot, so a flush copies nothing. Premise reproduced: the window staged in a Vec and flushed through the byte door. Decided: the slot is taken at the frame's open, not at batch_start; occupancy is one slot per conduit, not one per window as the brief said, because conduits stage independently; a slot short of the batch budget is refused, so the wire stays the heap stage's byte for byte; a dry pool or a link that lends nothing stages on the heap, counted (batch_lend_counts); a conduit rerouted or a lender leaving the set copies the frame to the heap; reopen and link drop give the slot back. No MCU image enables batching; footprint delta 0.

carry_forward_bullets: Open after this round (clause (2) of runtime-zero-copy's UPDATE R3159-R3169), as of commit 1e31e22e on branch fapw:

1. MULTICAST is not on the pool. Its writer queue's item is the datagram session-core's multicast push already ALLOCATED (multicast_tx_push encodes each owned item, a boxed PushOwned and the rest, with the Vec-returning encode_frame_with_*_qos and hands MulticastTxQueue::enqueue a Vec); copying that vector into a slot at the queue would add a copy and save no allocation. Next step, in wz-session-core: give MulticastTxQueue a lend (as BoxedLinkDriver has), encode the frame into the lent slot inside push_frame with the same mtu and fragment fallback the unicast send_frame_lent uses, and only then switch MulticastTxPlane::open to datagram_outbound_channel(). The owned PushOwned items upstream of it are their own allocation and their own item.

2. SCE OWNER'S ITEM: the generated cobs_encode (sources/codecs/cobs_encode.scxml, sce:kind="algorithm") allocates on every allocating build, because SCE maps a bounded `bytes` variable to the profile's growable SceBytes (HeapBytes) and grows it push by push: 5 allocations for a 64-byte serial frame, 9 at the 1500-byte MTU. The fix is SCE's: give a bounded bytes var fixed storage (InlineBytes) or reserve its declared capacity. serial_tx_pool_allocations::the_generated_stuffer_still_allocates_on_an_allocating_build reds when it lands; the three serial tests then assert zero outright.

3. Library seams, stated and counted: quinn's send_datagram takes bytes::Bytes and Bytes::from_owner boxes its owner (1 allocation per QUIC datagram, no copy); tungstenite 0.24's Message::Binary owns a Vec<u8> (1 allocation and 1 copy per lent websocket message; the byte door hands its vector straight in). Removing the websocket one needs tungstenite's later Bytes payload (a dependency bump, OWNER).

4. Slot sizes and table counts are the pool SSOTs' (session_tx_pool_ap.scxml, session_tx_pool_ap_small.scxml), build-time with documented derivations; the per-link datagram budgets are runtime, derived from the queue shape (config transport/link/tx/queue/size/* and the link batch), clamped to the tables. A shape asking for more than the table is clamped, not grown (a runtime-sized pool emit is an SCE question).

5. Behaviour change to watch under runtime-zero-copy (in preset-ap-full): a datagram link's in-flight datagrams are now bounded by its slot budget (an established UDP session without QoS: 3 small + 2 large), so a burst of tiny droppable datagrams faster than the writer meets congestion sooner than under the byte bound alone. This is the bound in datagrams that zenoh's two batches per priority hold; hosted runs of the UDP chaos and reliable suites under the preset are the check.

6. Rewrite the atom reason through the store: clause (2) built for the stream links, serial, UDP, QUIC datagram and websocket, with items 1 to 3 as its residue; move the depth pin and the reason-review pins (lib.rs and session_rx_pool_ap.rs rows carry R3250 as the placeholder round id) in that commit.

Round 3239.decision_summary: runtime-zero-copy clause (2) of UPDATE R3159-R3169, re-measured first: it reproduced (lent burst of 12 small frames 8 allocations, 4 frames of 20 KiB 4, byte door 1 per frame). Built: under runtime-zero-copy a stream or serial link's writer queue owns its own generated transmit pool (new SSOT session_tx_pool_ap, 16 x 65600, one per link), and the queue item is a slot handle walking the pool's transmit arms (acquire, arm on take, start at write, complete when the write ended, un-arm or return when abandoned). Frames pack back to back in a lane's newest slot, so the byte bound the lanes already apply needs few slots; a dry pool is back-pressure (no room for a data message, a wait for transport frames), never an allocation. Oversize is impossible by construction (slot holds 4 + u16::MAX). Serial: the queue now carries the framed wire, COBS-encoded into the slot; the generated COBS stuffer still allocates internally (SCE emit), pinned by test. carry_forward_bullets: 1. The AP UDP group link has no carrier detection. Measured in a sudo netns: a socket bound (SO_BINDTODEVICE) to a dummy device that is then deleted gets no recv error (recvfrom only times out) while a send gets ENODEV. UdpDriver::poll_event reports LinkLost only on a recv error, and the multicast transmit task treats a failed send as non-fatal, so neither the router group face nor the --sessions group session ever re-joins after an interface loss in practice; the re-join loop is reached only by a recv error. The MCU loop reads the netif LINK_UP bit (R2390); the AP side has no equivalent. Next step: give the UDP multicast link a carrier source (a failed group send with ENODEV/ENETDOWN, or an rtnetlink link-state watch on the iface) that surfaces as LinkEvent::Lost, then add the process-level netns test (delete/re-add the device mid-run, expect `link lost` then `rejoined` and a new `peer arrived`) in Layer M.
2. Hosted-only: the coordinator's preflight should confirm feature_public_surface_census and C1bz for wz-runtime-tokio (two new pub items in multicast_glue, GroupRejoin and rejoin_group_driver).

Round 3248.decision_summary: The C1cc red of 18ec8d78 (run 38079069289) is the REFERENCE arm of LEG 5, upstream z_get_shm.c on the real libzenohc: it printed the Talc refusal and then stood with its main thread in a futex wait until the 180 s bound. Not a wz defect, not a slow runner, not this wave: the 17 completed runs before it passed the leg in 2.4 s, the parent commit included, and the red commit touched nothing the leg runs. Cause: z_shm_provider_default_new leaves its out-parameter uninitialised on the error path and the example does not check, so the next call reads stack garbage; the allocation path locks mutexes inside the provider, so a stale pointer becomes a lock that never frees. The usual ending is SIGSEGV (300 of 300 local runs). Decided: classify, not lengthen. Bounded runs can hand a stall back, and LEG 5 accepts a reference stall only after the refusal; the wz arm and LEG 6 still fail on any stall. No bound changed.

On the MCU in-place path a Fragment cost 6 allocations per non-final turn and 10 at completion (unit copied, payload copied, heap staging, message copied into owned records); a lean lowlatency unit took the copying path (5 for one Put); a Frame with its own ext chain owned it every frame. A fragment's head is read in place (chain kept as header bytes), its payload copied once into its slot, and a completed message is read IN the slot, record by record. The observer gets a borrowed range descriptor (InPlaceFragment) instead of Poll(Fragment). Lowlatency units and Frame chains are read in place too; a chain is owned only for an owned record.

Round 3258.decision_summary: The coordinator chose option A, the root fix. The admin node now negotiates a batch of 1472 bytes, where it used 1500. The code works it out where the constant sits: ETHERNET_MTU 1500 less the 20-byte IPv4 header and the 8-byte UDP header. A router takes the smaller of its batch and the node's (upstream open.rs, batch_size.min). So no datagram of either session, in either direction, needs IP fragmentation, and HW.30 and HW.35 stay as written. The grammar still says that a 1500 batch could need fragments, and it now says the node negotiates 1472 so that none does. HW.35's burst limit stays in the grammar, stated as unmeasured. lwIP holds at most 8 lent frames, and its reassembly holds fragments addressed to the node for up to 15 s, so a burst or such fragments can be copied in and refused with nothing wrong in the slot path. No test pinned 1500, so there was no red-first pair to show; the constant is only an input to the handshake and to a link's receive capacity.

Round 3261.decision_summary: The accept-burst allocation witness of the AP UDP receive was flaky under load, and the cause was two things, not one. (1) Harness: the count was process-wide, so sibling tests, libtest threads and the acceptor worker moved it; it is now attributed per measurement (thread-local Tally on the test thread, on every thread of a test-owned runtime, and on the process-wide acceptor worker, which a measurement adopts) with one lock held for each test's whole body, and two controls pin the adoption and the exclusion. (2) Product: tokio's bounded mpsc between the demux pump and each accepted face allocates a block (Block::grow) from the pump's try_send when the pump runs further ahead than before, inside the zero-allocation receive. The channel is replaced by FaceQueue, a Mutex<VecDeque> plus Notify, sized to UDP_DEMUX_FACE_CHANNEL_CAP when the face opens under runtime-zero-copy, so a push never grows it. Semantics kept: drop on full, reap on closed, drain after sender drop. Nothing loosened.

Cause measured, not guessed: not a race and not a runner difference. The leg turns on transport-stats, and under it wz-session-core keeps the owned record form (RECORD_FORM in drive.rs: its counters classify the owned message), so a lean Put read in place is decoded owned: three allocations (key expression, payload, owned Push), shown by a backtrace of the failing window. The test asserted the zero-heap rule of a build WITHOUT the counters and ran in a lane WITH them. It failed 160 of 160 runs on pc2 before. Round 3266.decision_summary: Open-debt item 902 reproduced, and wider than the register says: not only the multicast group link but every wz datagram link (unicast dial, accepted demux face, UdpDriver group and scouting) reported a lost link from a failed READ only. In a netns, deleting the device a socket is bound to leaves recvfrom silent while every send fails; the writer task logged and returned, and the multicast transmit task counted the datagram unwritten and went on. Upstream has no carrier watch either: its UDP link maps io errors to ZResult, and the transport ends the link at the first TX or RX task error (unicast universal link.rs, multicast link.rs delete). So wz mirrors that rather than adding an rtnetlink watch: a failed send trips a per-link latch (DatagramWriteFault) which the read driver's poll_event races first and reports as LinkEvent::Lost OsError. Faces of one listener keep separate latches. Any send error trips it, as upstream's does. Deviation from the register: no rtnetlink path.

Round 3268.decision_summary: The intermittent unixpipe lib-test hang (three stray test processes on the build hosts) reproduced at about 40 percent of runs of the unixpipe_pipeline filter and has TWO causes, both fixed at the cause, no timeout. (1) The two-dialer test paired each dialer link with the acceptor link in accept order; racing dialers arrive in either order, so about half the runs sent a frame on one FIFO pair and awaited it on the other, forever. It now pairs by the dedicated nodes and asserts that first. (2) bind_unixpipe registered the request channel with the BINDER's reactor but read it on the acceptor runtime; when the binder's runtime ended every read failed at once and the acceptor retried without yielding, holding the process's one acceptor thread (about 3 percent of runs). The channel is now registered inside the acceptor task, and a non-InvalidData read error ends the acceptor. unixsock and serial have neither pattern; udp demux shares (2) with a bounded symptom (carry).

carry_forward_bullets: Consumers that stored census documents or reports made before this fix hold wrong roles for nodes named only by an INIT or JOIN (a peer as router, a client as peer; routers were right). Nodes named by a Hello were always right, and the first message to name a node sets its role. Census revision was deliberately not bumped (the header's rules cover renamed or removed keys and widened closed string vocabularies; a numeric key with an unchanged meaning and a corrected value is a bug fix), so a document cannot say which side of the fix it is on. If the owner wants a consumer-visible marker, the lever is a census revision bump with an unchanged key set (precedent: revision 4, which changed no key), which touches wz_dissect.h, doc_revision.rs and the ABI gates that another worker is editing now; that is an owner decision, not made here. The consumer-facing analyzer team should be told that stored role values from earlier captures are suspect.

The hand-laid INIT and JOIN fixtures in node.rs (init_wire, join_message) write a cbyte of (len - 1) << 4 | 0x02, a client. They are valid fixtures and now read as a client; nothing else in the tree asserts a census role for an INIT or a JOIN, so the new sweep is the only guard on it.

Round 3269.decision_summary: The passive census read a handshake role as (cbyte >> 1) & 0x03 for INIT and JOIN; the codec, the SCE sources and upstream (flags & 0b11, zid_len_m1 in the top nibble) put it in the LOW two bits. Found by a read-through survey, not by a test. Premise reproduced: a peer (cbyte 0x01) read as router, a client (0x02) as peer; a router read right only because 0 shifts to 0. Fixed at the cause: both arms call the decoded body's own whatami() accessor, the private mask is deleted, so the layout lives in one place. Nothing asserted nodes[].whatami for INIT or JOIN, so no fixture could fail; the module's own fixtures lay cbyte (len-1)<<4|0x02 and were read as peer unnoticed. Census revision: NOT bumped. The header's rules cover a renamed or removed key and a widened closed string vocabulary; whatami is a number whose meaning (0 router, 1 peer, 2 client) is unchanged, so a corrected value is a bug fix. Consumers holding revision-20 documents carry wrong roles for INIT/JOIN nodes.

Next step: forward the selector from the acceptor and admin-node shells (deploy/mcu-session-acceptor via wz-mcu-session-acceptor, deploy/mcu-admin-node, deploy/zephyr-admin-node), run each image's Layer Q case and read its stack: peak line; the lent encode adds frames and the InitAck mint adds a 144-byte array plus a 16-byte zid array on the stack. The wz facade has no forward for it (as for bounded-heapless), so an image names wz-session-core directly.

2. Still on the heap under the profile, outside this step: (a) multicast TX (multicast_tx.rs Box items and Vec frames, multicast_drive.rs JOIN/Close datagrams): no lend seam; (b) every sender that takes an owned message the CALLER builds (send_push_aliased, Del, with_meta, Request, Response, Declare, Interest): the send is lent but the owned build is the caller's heap (S3/S5 owned-storage profile); (c) a Put under transport-stats keeps the owned build, because stats classify the owned form; (d) the block-first job copies the body to a Vec (schedule_block_first), only reachable with an installed hand-off, none on the MCU; (e) admin status JSON Strings (S9); (f) the session bundle itself: three Rc, SessionInitParams Vecs, ext chain Vecs, the boxed entropy source (S5). The acceptor's inbound_peer_zid and inbound_cookie slots are still Vec.

3. transport-compression and transport-multilink are not covered by the selector and under it become counted refusals (compression drops the frame; a lent batch moved off a leaving link is given up). An image that turns the selector on must not turn those on; no build error enforces it because --all-features lanes build both.

4. A stop marker or a fragment the link lends no slot for ends the chain: with fragments already on the wire the stop marker is attempted from a second lend and, if that is refused too, the peer holds its staged chain until its own reassembly timeout. Counted, not retried.
5. A refused send spends its SN (as a refused fragment chain already did). A retry is a new frame.
6. Owner decision: whether the refusal should surface to the application of a handshake (today the FSM action discards it, counted; the handshake deadline then closes the session).

7. Re-pin docs/reason-review-pins.md rows for wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs and wz-session-core/src/link.rs (runtime-zero-copy), and name S4 in the reason: clause "TX lend-only on the MCU, a refused lend an explicit LinkSendOutcome" now holds for the unicast profile.

Round 3280.decision_summary: Open-debt item 877 follow-up: the receive-resource-error reading of 2 on the first INCR4 boot of the first kit session is explained, and it is not the burst length. The counter counts frames that reach the MAC while all 8 receive descriptors are software-owned. Twelve counted boots (6 per image, alternating, same build apart from the burst value) read 2 errors in 5 boots, 4 INCR4 and 1 single-beat, and every one of the 5 coincided with a group of 10 broadcast frames sent by the bench host's own name-service daemon within 0.1 ms (10 minus the ring's 8 is 2); groups of 4, 5 and 6 gave 0. Controlled bursts of N frames gave about N minus 8 on both images (N=9 about 1, N=64 about 54 versus 47); a quiet link and eight boots with a 200 frames per second stream from link-up gave 0. No product code changes. Not measured: a power-off start, INCR8/16.
verification_bullets: Measured on 2026-10-11 (KST 16:54 to 18:10) on the T2G kit (CYT4BF8CEE rev B2, KitProg3 serial 171C033C03272400, 100 Mbps full duplex to a bench host) by the lab role, an agent session, with the owner's permission for hardware writes (2026-10-10, repeated 2026-10-11). Nothing else held the console or the probe (checked before every flash and boot).

Images (a controlled pair, both with both pool overlays, west build from the same source path, Zephyr 4.4.99, SDK 1.0.1): single-beat = origin/main f90a4874, DMA_CONFIG 0x01180701: ELF sha256 a36cddb8660ecd9a2327cd2e702348e6c31779ac5c35322d510cf6eb310efd89, M7_0 region 0x10080000 sha256 b07e5b0fdf8ff20d65c7c94a56f18844f5ef974555658728ee6a6c6324e2f33a. INCR4 = f90a4874 plus the burst default commit c0ee9d7d and its doc commit fca53a92 (cherry-picked), DMA_CONFIG 0x01180704: ELF sha256 5d15a820198ec049c23a6f04366727e32540451e367d40f4512f7967a67c757d, region sha256 524c165a276278b7e38b7e410a016f6b25d3534a73d07675ccfbc47bd2778b4d. The two regions differ in exactly 3 bytes (the burst constant 1 to 4 in the MAC config code and two low bytes of the build-time literal). CM0+ launcher unchanged and not written: region sha256 7d85cf4584b024019a76846ceb4445325418e73a7091cae43be08e4fa5d3d84b, ELF sha256 e3fb83c72f27a481889795d62194b83596475a226f7f4b26809be4ce26eb2c91. Router: the pinned zenohd (v1211779c, binary sha256 a6a8cb094efffa9ccfcc34af790aa3322899a7e295ea4aedc0ff0afc0a195257). Verdict program scripts/lib/admin_node_verdict.py sha256 1096717853c884db782db93e4aab2be5fcb3af1a1de878573ef98c498ac63c65 (identical on main and on the bench).

Method. Before the first write both regions were read without a reset: CM0+ 7d85cf45..., M7 7902b54e0cccd068ee541a1694ee6d43e3131c072dd99b99241a05e3381c9e30, the saved original CM0+ image hashed bee8c20af0bb3643f78e69be2f93f8fe04c6b8e4457761c2995a6b65a6acd1b9. Each image was written to the M7_0 region with program and verify (flasher Verified OK each time, nothing at 0x10000000), then the boot under test was a debugger reset run, with the counters read through the debugger without a halt: the whole 46-word MAC statistics block (read-to-clear, so every read is a delta), NETWORK_CONTROL, DMA_CONFIG, RECEIVE_Q_PTR, RECEIVE_STATUS and the 8 receive descriptors' used bits, about every 74 ms for the first 45 s and every second after, to 150 s, each sample stamped; console lines stamped per line; a capture of every frame on the board's adapter. Window: 0 to 25 s quiet (the host has no address on the board's subnet), at 25 s the host address is added, at 30 s a 10 frames per second ping (400 byte payload) and the program's board mode (the eight onboard sentences), then the stock router holds a session to 150 s; from 110 s a calibration burst series (see below). Twelve counted boots, INCR4 first, alternating, 6 per image; one pilot boot of each kind was run first and is not counted. The pilot of the sampler (single image, 100 s) and a second pilot with the bursts are kept apart.

Results. (1) Quiet window, 12 of 12 boots: 0 frames reached the node and 0 resource errors. (2) Natural resource errors outside the calibration bursts: INCR4 boots b01 b03 b07 b11 read 2 each (b05 b09 read 0), single-beat b10 read 2 (b02 b04 b06 b08 b12 read 0); Fisher exact p = 0.24 for 4 of 6 against 1 of 6. Cumulative at the asked marks: at +10 s all 12 boots read 0; at +30 s only b01 read 2 (at 28.04 s), the others 0; the other four came at 61.5, 83.6, 91.2 and 92.3 s (so were in the +120 s mark, which also holds the first calibration bursts from 110 s). Every one of the 5 events falls in the sample that follows a group of 10 broadcast frames from the host (NetBIOS name queries, one group of 6, then 10, then 5 at about 2 s spacing, seen in 5 boots, 4 INCR4 and 1 single-beat, at 26 to 28 s after the address was added in b01 and at 58 to 92 s in the others); the groups of 6, 5 and 4 frames in the same boots gave 0; no resource error occurred without a group of 10, and no group of 10 without 2. (3) Calibration bursts (21 per boot of N minimum-size frames sent back to back to the node's address, spread of 0.03 to 0.2 ms at the host; valid in b03 to b12, 15 bursts per N per image, b01 and b02 went to a stale station address and are excluded): resource errors per burst, INCR4 against single-beat: N=4 0 and 0; N=8 2 of 15 bursts nonzero (1 each) and 3 of 15; N=9 14 and 15 in total over 15 bursts; N=12 61 and 56; N=16 114 and 122; N=32 338 and 339 (mean 22.5 and 22.6, the maximum 24 each); N=64 805 and 701 (mean 53.7 and 46.7; Mann-Whitney permutation p = 0.15, no difference shown). The maximum per burst is N minus 8 on both images. (4) Boot-race: 8 boots, 4 per image, with a 200 frames per second broadcast stream running through the acquire and the reset, so frames are on the wire from the link-up at about 2.03 s on the console; the first frame was counted 2.10 to 2.11 s after the reset; 0 resource errors in 8 of 8 boots, about 3590 frames counted each, at most 2 descriptors software-owned at any sample. (5) The pool's own counts: refused 0, dropped 0, copied 0 on the last counts line of all 12 counted boots. (6) RECEIVE_Q_PTR, DMA_CONFIG 0x01180701 or 0x01180704 as built, TRANSMIT_STATUS without an AMBA error in every sample.

Judging call of the first session (both pool flags, from files): in all 12 counted boots 7 steps ended OK (HW.26, HW.29 to HW.31, HW.33 to HW.35) and 3 ended FAIL (HW.27, HW.28, HW.32) with the program's own message that the console holds 2 pool lines where one boot prints one. That is a harness artifact of this experiment, not of the images: each counted console file holds two Zephyr boot banners, one from the boot the debugger's acquire starts after a fresh flash without reset (the first session flashed with a reset and had one) and one from the reset under test; the three failed steps read the pool placement and last descriptor against one pool line. The two pilot boots, run on an image already booted once, hold one banner and judged all ten OK. The measured counters are unaffected: the sampler's reset stamp is the boot under test.

Code reading before the experiment: Cyt4bfMac::bring_up arms all 8 receive descriptors (init_rx_ring) and writes the queue pointer before it writes NETWORK_CONTROL with receive enabled, so no frame can meet an unarmed descriptor at enable; the receiver then sees no link until the PHY's renegotiation finishes (console 2.03 s). The register is read-to-clear (the vendor register macros give it a clear-on-read mask of 0x3ffff); the vendor driver reads it as a statistic. The driver never reads RX_RESOURCE_ERRORS, and clears RECEIVE_STATUS bit 0 itself, so only the statistics register keeps the count.

Restore: the M7_0 region was written back from the region read before the first write (flasher Verified OK), then both regions were read back by a separate dump: CM0+ 7d85cf4584b024019a76846ceb4445325418e73a7091cae43be08e4fa5d3d84b and M7_0 7902b54e0cccd068ee541a1694ee6d43e3131c072dd99b99241a05e3381c9e30, equal to the values before the first write; the saved original image still hashes bee8c20af0bb3643f78e69be2f93f8fe04c6b8e4457761c2995a6b65a6acd1b9. One reset boot of the restored image printed core clock 350000000 Hz, link up at 100 Mbps and the READY line. No debugger, capture or ping process and no console reader was left running; the host address on the board's subnet was removed.

NOT measured: the first session's boot itself (it had no capture of broadcast frames, so that its 2 was a group of 10 is inferred from the match of mechanism and count, not observed); a start after the board's power was removed (the boots are debugger resets); whether the host's name-service group of 10 occurs at power-on of a different host; INCR8 and INCR16; throughput and latency; the time spacing of burst frames on the wire (the USB adapter's); any receive error other than resource errors (frame check, alignment and overrun counters read 0 throughout). Statistics are small: 6 boots per image; the INCR4 versus single difference in who saw a group of 10 (4 of 6 against 1 of 6) is a property of when the host's daemon spoke and is not significant (p 0.24).

Round 3282.decision_summary: The hosted C1bn red (udp_chaos_e2e, 'recovery Put not delivered within the ~6s budget') is a pre-existing test defect, not a regression and not a slow poll. It reproduces on 6c55e873 and on 2658d13c alike (1 in 100 unloaded each; 22% vs 26% with 8 copies on 2 cores, no significant difference), and no congestion or writer-queue code moved between them. Cause, measured with transport stats on an instrumented build: the datagram lane holds 2 frames and a droppable Put waits wait_before_drop (1 ms) for the writer task; the tests publish two oversize Puts back to back with the default Drop policy, so the recovery Put is congestion-dropped before it leaves the sender (stats read one dropped message in all 14 failing reorder runs; the acceptor saw no datagram of it). Repair: both Puts of the three chaos tests use CongestionControl::Block. The timeout is untouched. 0 of 208 runs fail under the same contention afterwards; a mutant that sends the recovery Put nowhere is red in all three tests.

Round 3283.decision_summary: The red test is a wrong premise in the test, not a product defect. It bound the session socket, whose queue depth is a profile constant (16 default, 4 under buffer-pool-session-rx-slim). A queue of Q holds Q-1 datagrams and a socket that holds lent frames keeps them in that queue, so the slim socket is full at its third held frame (3) and never reaches the shim's bound of 8 (RX_HELD_MAX). The product behaves correctly there: the full queue refuses the frame, counts it and returns the slot. Fix: the test shapes its socket from the shim's bound (queue RX_HELD_MAX+2, const-asserted to outlast the bound) so it means the same on every profile, plus a control for the shallow-queue case. CI never ran this lib at the slim profile (only clippy compiled it): one C1n leg added.

Round 3288.decision_summary: The hosted C1bn red of b4f30b18 (uring_reactor two_frames_of_one_completion_are_ranges_of_its_slot, 63 vs 64) is a product ordering defect that CPU contention exposes, not a regression and not a leak. deliver_completion sent the delivery from inside the function that still held the worker's own Arc on the completion's slot, so the slot came home only when the worker thread was scheduled again after the send. Measured: with 8 copies on 2 cores the unchanged code fails 25 percent of single-test runs on both 6c55e873 and b4f30b18 (no difference), 0 of 150 unloaded; an instrumented copy always reads 63 first and 64 within 5 ms (50 ms when a 50 ms sleep is injected after the send), never leaked. Fix: completion_delivery takes the frame by value and returns the Delivery, so the worker holds nothing on the slot when the link can see the delivery; the send follows. The test needs no wait. A witness reads the pool at that instant; a leak mutant and a late-hold mutant both redden it.

Round 3289.decision_summary: S9a moves every table a peer writes, or that is owed to one peer, out of the process-wide observer into the per-session slot (decision Q7, per session; application registries stay process-wide). Chosen over a shared table with a session key: a wire alias id is session-scoped, so a shared table lets two peers collide on one id, and a flood by one peer would exhaust the others; a per-slot table makes both impossible by construction, and a release forgets the table in place. Each registry is now an application table plus one peer side (Deref and wrapper methods keep the AP API unchanged). Under bounded-heapless every peer table is a fixed table that refuses the entry past its bound, counts the refusal and allocates nothing; replies and finals are fallible (ReplyError StagingFull, PayloadTooLarge) and a request whose Final cannot be owed is refused before a queryable runs. Default and AP builds keep growable tables and behave as before.

Round 3295.decision_summary: The hosted C1cc red (an open that returned after 105 ms where a listener 400 ms late was expected) was not a double hand-out by the free_port ledger. The kernel re-handed the number free_port had released to another test's own bind(:0): since a peer open binds tcp/[::]:0 by default, 8 of the 11 legs of connect_retry_open open a session whose listener draws from the same pool. That listener then answered the client's dial, or took the number the late listener needed (z_open -4), or cut a peer's start window short. Decision: free_port and the child port reservation draw from a range the kernel never autoselects from (probed by an explicit bind), and every number handed out is also an flock claim, so two test processes drawing from the same range cannot hold one number. Not done: loosening the 400 ms bound or adding retries. The register text for this red guessed a shared number or an early bind; the measurement showed a third cause.
verification_bullets: All builds and runs on the pc3 and hkl002 build hosts through bx; contention runs pin 24 concurrent copies of a test binary to 2 cores (taskset), 40 rounds, 960 runs per side.

Cause: 32 free_port holders beside 8 threads binding [::]:0 got 17.6k of 3.9M binds on a handed-out number (0.45%); a late-listener loop beside 8 peer-session open/close threads gave 7 early opens (110-317 ms) in 1500 legs, 0 in 150 without the churn.

Before: connect_retry_open failed 22 of 960 and 21 of 960 runs. After: 0 of 960 twice, the second time on the final tree. Base and branch lib binaries of wz-runtime-tokio-test-support under the same contention: base 0 of 960 each time; branch 0 of 960 on the final tree.

Integration found three defects in the repair itself, each measured and fixed in this push. (1) The claim for every handed-out number is held until the process exits, and two tests of the crate drew 256 numbers each: 24 copies exhausted the 8192-number range and 916 of 960 lib runs panicked; the two tests now take 32 numbers, the ledger is witnessed with no claim, and the exhaustion panic says whether binds or claims refused the draws. (2) The claim test killed a holder and re-claimed its number in the shared registry, a race against every other picker: 16 of 960; it now uses a registry of its own. (3) The refusing-port test failed 26 of 80 unpinned runs against 0 of 80 on base: a process started by a sibling test holds a just-dropped listener open between fork and exec (87 of 100 beside the holder test, 58 of 100 beside the probe process, 0 of 100 beside the tests that start none); a spawn gate fixes it, 0 of 100 after.

Round 3325.decision_summary: The close verb of the session lifecycle is also a QUERY. A GET on @/<zid>/<whatami>/session/close/<peer-zid> orders every link of that peer's session closed and is answered with a verdict (closing with the link count, already_closed, not_found, or refused with a reason); a GET on @/<zid>/<whatami>/session/verbs answers the verbs the node has. Round 3375.decision_summary: The transmit and receive buffer pools of the T2G admin node were measured on silicon for what they do to round-trip time, and no gain that the samples can attribute to them was found. Four images of one source tree (no pool, transmit pool, receive pool, both) were each booted twice; the medians of a REST query round trip are 5.00, 5.04, 4.90 and 4.92 ms, and every difference is about one kernel tick (0.1 ms at 10000 ticks a second) and flips between boots of the same image. This agrees with the August arithmetic that a 1.5 KB copy costs about 4 microseconds at 350 MHz, so the pool is a correctness and substitutability result and not a speed one. NOT claimed: that the pools are slower or faster, any comparison with zenoh-pico on this board (none was ever run there), the node's CPU time per datagram (the firmware has no counter), or the cause of the 5 ms floor of a query round trip (ICMP is 0.75 ms), for which only a hypothesis exists.
verification_bullets: Per boot: 2000 ICMP echoes of 56 B and of 1400 B, and 1500 REST GETs of the status key and of the config key through a stock router that dials the node; every sample kept, none lost, no bad reply, the core clock read 350 MHz and each boot's capture held one boot.

Medians in ms, base / transmit pool / receive pool / both: ICMP 56 B 0.7495 / 0.7530 / 0.7520 / 0.7820; ICMP 1400 B 1.260 / 1.130 / 1.270 / 1.240; GET status 5.0015 / 5.0413 / 4.9023 / 4.9249; GET config 4.7641 / 4.8193 / 4.7008 / 4.7003. Per boot, the transmit-pool GET status medians are 5.004 and 5.097 and the both-pools ones 4.902 and 4.998, so the boot-to-boot spread equals the differences.

A bootstrap over the pooled samples gave intervals that call some of these faster or slower; they treat samples as independent and two boots per image is too few for that to hold, so they are not a finding. The 1400 B echo of the transmit-pool image is 130 us under base in both boots although an echo never crosses the transmit pool and the other two images show nothing: not attributable.
Restore: both regions read back by a separate dump equal the saved originals (CM0+ bee8c20a, M7_0 16c4e4d7), and the restored kit boots the OEM image.
NOT verified: the node's CPU time per datagram; more than two boots per image; any comparison with the reference stack on this board.

Round 3378.decision_summary: The performance loop's third batch: an opt-in receive busy-poll and a defect its test found. A deadline wake now takes one waiting frame first. NOT claimed: that wz is faster than pico (by default it is not: 22 against 19 us, the responder at 2.2 times pico's cycles), receive against pico, other payload sizes, the MCU, the hosted run.

Round 3379.decision_summary: The selector language reaches every field of a record's dissection. A word that is no fixed field is a dotted path into the tree the field document shows (qos.priority, put.encoding.id, source_info.zid), written from the message or as any tail, resolved at parse against a declared shape, wz_session_core::dissect_schema, whose test walks seeded noise over every message id and fails on a walked path it lacks. An extension is named by its ext_name, the chain is not a level, a named entry's header fields stand under ext. A path alone tests presence. A walked message lacking the field is a decided no, != its negation; an unwalked record is undecided. A tail ending fields of two kinds is refused with longer tails; an unknown word names the five nearest. in / not in, matches (feature filter-regex, regex-automata on alloc), key contains and len() join. wz_dissect_selector_fields (ABI 44) lists it all; selector_diagnose moves to 5.

Round 3380.decision_summary: Every row of the field and selection documents is judged. A row plane (crates/wz-capture/src/row_plane.rs), run once per capture beside the census planes, judges what they leave: a Declare, Interest or network Oam in a batch, a transport message with no batch, and a ResponseFinal whose request is missing. RecordView.kind becomes a three-state Record: a kind; None, a row with no record, where every term about a record is decided as an absent field (no, and yes under != or not); Unread, the orphan close, where they are undecided and dir is the requester's. A halted batch adds an undecided record. Unjudged is left to undecodable rows and ambiguous selectors. Ten row facts join the language: msg (any message the row rode in), src, dst, addr (IP with prefix, MAC, vsock cid), sport, dport, port, link, flow and packet. flow is the document's list_id, printed on every flow object and read per document against a live handle's numbering.

Round 3381.decision_summary: Arbitrary UDP no longer stands as zenoh. The passive reader refuses an Init or a Join announcing a protocol version other than 0x09 (new wire_const::PROTOCOL_VERSION, InboundParseError::ForeignVersion), and the capture's scouting decode does the same for a Scout or a Hello; a participant's decode keeps upstream's order. The byte alone is one chance in 256, measured: a random datagram opened as a Join of 0x09. So every PassiveFrame carries unit_read_whole, and only a unit read whole (every message decoded, every byte accounted for) counts as evidence or names a node, an initiator or an acceptor. VersionEvidence counts own-version messages in whole units and foreign-version ones anywhere; flows and session rows carry zenoh: proven, unproven, foreign_version or mixed. A session joined after its handshake is unproven, as arbitrary bytes are.

Round 3383.decision_summary: The selector verdict (selector_diagnose 7) gives each token the role the parser read it as: field, path, operator, value, function, logic or group, a family closed by @values. The lexer's kind cannot say it: in, contains and matches are words that fill an operator's slot, a list's values are words, len is a word naming a function, and the not of not in is half an operator. A consumer colouring a selector would otherwise rebuild the parser. A role is written when the parser reads a token into its slot, so it is ABSENT where the parser did not reach: past a refusal, over a selector the lexer refused, and on a word in a field's slot that names neither a field nor a path, since the lookup decides which and refused both. A value the field then refuses keeps role value. Brackets are all group. kind does not move.

Round 3425.decision_summary: A consumer with no registered organization number cannot use a Custom Option, which needs one. The pcapng format reserves option codes with the top bit set for local use and asks for no registration, so the consumer records what it knows about a packet in one and must read it back. wz_dissect_pcap_local_options_of_link_type (ABI 49) returns, on the packets of a link type, every option with a code of 0x8000 or above, joined to the packets by number, as 32-byte records: packet, offset, len, index, code, big_endian. It is a door of its own and not a mode of the Custom Option door: the two sets cannot overlap (the four Custom codes are below 0x8000), and a local code has no organization number, no text flag and no copy flag. The format states a copy rule for the Custom Options and none for a local code, so a field for it would invent one. A local code is not unique among files by other applications, so the code alone names nothing; the value is the writer's and is carried unread.

A lifecycle peer's zid derives from the public key of the credential it authenticates with (the public-key extension or TLS); only an authenticated peer may command a verb. Round 3458.decision_summary: Record the owner's ruling of 2026-10-23 on the lifecycle credential (decision D9 of docs/session-lifecycle-intent.md, cost not counted): a lifecycle verb is taken only over a secure channel, and every profile uses one protocol for it, TLS 1.3 with mutual authentication. Each side signs the transcript, so the dialling side is proven too, and every frame is protected under keys that handshake derived. The key travels in a self-signed certificate and is trusted by pinning the zid derived from it. The fixed-memory profile gets a TLS 1.3 stack in static memory behind the same port, Mbed TLS 3.6 LTS being the candidate measured first. The ruling follows a measured defect in step 1a: a public-key proof over TCP is not bound to the frames after the handshake, so it stops counting for the verbs. REMAINING is unchanged.

Round 3471.decision_summary: Make a unicast datagram link's peer its identity, fixed once known. The MCU UDP links (coop over BSD-style sockets, and lwIP) sent their replies to the source of the last datagram they took, so one datagram from another address pointed an established session's replies and keep-alives at that address until the peer spoke again; on the kit one stray stalled a session for about twenty seconds. wz_session_core::datagram_peer now decides this once for both drivers, as upstream's UDP link does with a connected socket and a link per source: a dialled link is bound from the dial, an accepting link by the first InitSyn it takes, and a bound link hands its session only the peer's datagrams, discarding and counting strays and other sources' InitSyns. A driver on a listener's shared socket leaves another session's datagram in place.

Round 3477.decision_summary: Round 3473 bounded a session loop's turn at eight events, but an event is not a unit: one that carries thirty records costs thirty times one record. The turn is now eight records. An event pays a unit for each record it carries, one for an event with none, and an event that overdraws the turn yields once for each whole quantum it overdrew: deficit round robin with the run queue as the round, so every session has the same share of its thread whatever its frames hold. The bound in the code, 0.7 s for 2048 sessions, used an assumed 2 us an event and is replaced: an event of one record measures 6.5 to 11 us on a build host, which makes the return 2.1 to 3.6 s on a twentieth of a core against the 10 s lease. A test holds the property with no clock: one thread, an endless backlog, a second task woken in the middle runs within eight events, and the same flood without the loop's yield does not. The E7s binary passes and the cost table did not move beside the previous loop.

Round 3478.decision_summary: The cooperative profile gets a TCP link, written once in wz-runtime-coop over a StreamSocket seam, as the datagram link already is. Step 2 of the owner's size-gap structure (one engine, one stream link, a thin C ABI). zenoh's stream framing is a u16 little-endian length inside the batch; the driver asks the session for two bytes of headroom and writes the length there, so length and batch leave in one write from the slot. A stream that ends (peer close, read error, a length over the buffer) ends the link: the receive stops, the pump asks the link whether it is lost, and the session is told through dispatch_link_lost. A dial now names its protocol: a Locator carries udp or tcp, and a stack without the link refuses with Unsupported, which the connect manager reads as permanent; a refused connect is Unreachable and retried. The host stack (IpStack) holds either link in one slot type. lwIP, Zephyr and the memory stack stay datagram-only and refuse tcp/ by name.

Round 3488.decision_summary: Open-debt item 924, D5 of docs/dissect-row-index.md decided (owner: long-term correct, cost not counted): one walk per call, and no cache of decoded rows between calls. The repeated reads step 4b measured are scans (exchange pairing, declaration absorption, census planes), and a bounded cache gets no hit on a scan longer than it is under any policy, while one that holds the scan holds the capture decoded; the textbook answer is a shared scan, the reference dissector's tap model. Rows are immutable, a lookup by position decodes one unit, and a cache between calls would put a lock in a no_std store and take Sync from Dissection. Applied: the field document's declaration absorption rides on the exchange pairing's walk through ordered_fold::Share whenever both readers' own rules pick the same messages, and walks alone otherwise. Each row is decoded three times per consumer pass instead of four; field windows cost +12% and +11% over the build before 4b instead of +19% and +22%.

Round 3495.decision_summary: The secure channel's receive record buffer is the protocol's maximum, 2^14 bytes, and its send buffer stays at 1,500. The record size limit of RFC 8449 is the only protocol bound on what a peer sends. rustls 0.23, which zenohd 1.10.1 links, does not implement it, and zenoh's TLS link leaves rustls's fragment size at 16 kB. That a zenoh peer's data records stay within the negotiated batch is an implementation's behaviour, not a bound. rustls also sends a whole handshake flight as one record, sized by the certificate the peer presents. The send side is ours: the largest record this end wrote on the kit was 341 B, against a data record of at most a 1,024 B batch plus its 2-byte length. Shrinking the receive buffer through the limit with peers that implement it is a later saving, not a bound to rely on.
verification_bullets: T2G kit through the kit lane on pc2 (preflight, build, run): `TLS-FIT done ok=1 rounds=3`, the wrong-zid round refused. Sources read for the bound: rustls 0.23.40 and 0.23.43 (no record size limit; HandshakeFlight; max_fragment_size default 16 kB), zenoh 1.10.1 zenoh-link-tls (MTU 65535, fragment size untouched) and unicast establishment (min of both batches).

Round 3502.decision_summary: The fixed-memory profile's secure channel sits behind the cooperative runtime's stream port as a stream over a stream. The port is split in two: StreamSocket is the I/O of a connected stream and StreamDial is a value the stack holds to open one, so what a dial needs besides an address (an identity) belongs to the dial and the stream link stays written once. The backend is its own crate, wz-tls-mbedtls, over the Mbed TLS revision the Zephyr workspace pins, carried as two submodules and built through its own CMake with a configuration that states the kit image's choices. Its C side keeps every Mbed TLS structure in the static arena and Rust holds only pointers, so no layout crosses the boundary. Against a rustls server built the way zenohd 1.10.1 builds its mutual-TLS server, a device pinned by its own self-signed certificate is admitted and a stranger's pin refuses it.

Every list reads its units from a byte source, and a row names its bytes by a locator kept apart from its anchor: a stream range, or a place in a unit log. A list of datagrams logs each unit's payload once, in a chunked byte log that never reallocates, or remembers its place in a lent container and keeps no copy; a discard that takes a unit's last row releases its bytes. One 48-byte row layout serves every list, a row kept whole being a flag on it. A UDP or raweth datagram borrows its payload from its packet. Steps left: the serial line, recovered QUIC, WebSocket and TLS plaintext and the scouting rows, then the memory gate. Round 3505.decision_summary: A tls/ locator names a stream link inside the secure channel of D9, and a stack carries that channel only when it is given one. LinkProto gains Tls; IpStack and IpLinks take a third, secure-stream dial through with_tls, whose default is a dial that carries nothing. Without a channel a tls/ dial is Unsupported, decided before any buffer is claimed, so a stack whose tables happen to be full never reports a protocol it lacks as Exhausted and retried. A stream names its own protocol (StreamSocket::PROTO), so the link's endpoints read tls/ over a channel and the stream link stays written once. The locator parser takes tls/; whether a stack can dial it is the stack's answer, not the parser's. Also repaid: Layer 0's shellcheck red from Round 3491, where the D2 guard's text sat in single quotes with backticks.

Round 3507.decision_summary: The hosted run of the capacity promise failed: in the E7s job of CI run 40066938187 (tip 2ea53d076) 308 admitted client sessions ended on their own. The cause is the recorded keepalive cost: 10 us is one machine's figure, and the hosted runner serves a forwarded message in 46 to 52 us where the build host reads 12 to 13, so 1100 sessions were admitted on a host that holds about a quarter of that. A constant recorded on one host is not a promise about another. The router now measures the cost on its own host: every keepalive emission is timed, the first 64 sessions of a process emit once at establishment so the figure exists before a burst is over, and the lower decile of the window, given the room the recorded cost has over it (220 percent), bounds admission when it is dearer than the recorded cost. The first version used the median and was wrong: it swings with load and admitted 516 to 816 where 1100 fit.
